questions.q: What does kinematics study?
questions.e: Kinematics describes motion without analyzing the forces causing it.

questions.q: What is a reference point used for?
questions.e: Position and motion are specified relative to a reference point.

questions.q: When is an object at rest relative to an observer?
o: Its position does not change with time
questions.e: Rest is relative to an observer and means no change of position.

questions.q: Which example illustrates relative rest?
o: A seated passenger relative to the bus
A rotating fan blade relative to its frame
A falling stone relative to the road
A runner relative to the track
questions.e: A seated passenger maintains position relative to the bus.

questions.q: A passenger sitting in a moving bus is moving relative to what?
questions.e: The passenger changes position relative to the roadside tree.

questions.q: Which motion has no change in the orientation of the moving object?
questions.e: In pure translatory motion the body does not rotate.

questions.q: Which is an example of rotatory motion?
questions.e: The fan rotates around its axis.

questions.q: Which is an example of vibratory motion?
o: A train on a straight track
questions.e: The string moves back and forth about its mean position.

questions.q: A car moving along a straight road exhibits which translatory motion?
questions.e: Rectilinear motion follows a straight path.

questions.q: A car rounding a bend exhibits which translatory motion?
questions.e: Curvilinear motion follows a curved path.

questions.q: A butterfly changing direction unpredictably illustrates which motion?
questions.e: Random motion has an irregular, unpredictable path.

questions.q: Which part of a spinning fan undergoes circular motion around its axis?
questions.e: A point on the blade travels around the axis in a circle.

questions.q: What is distance?
o: Total length of the path traveled
questions.e: Distance is the length of the actual path followed.

questions.q: What is displacement?
o: Directed change from initial to final position
questions.e: Displacement specifies the change in position and direction.

questions.q: Which quantity is scalar?
Which quantity is a vector?
questions.e: Displacement has both magnitude and direction.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of displacement?
questions.e: Displacement is a length and is measured in metres.

questions.q: After completing one lap and returning to the start, displacement is:
Which is always true for a journey?
o: Distance is at least the magnitude of displacement
Displacement is always greater than distance
questions.e: The straight-line separation cannot exceed path length.

questions.q: When can distance equal displacement magnitude?
o: For motion along a straight line without reversing
questions.e: Straight one-direction motion follows the shortest path.

questions.q: Can displacement be negative along a chosen axis?
o: Yes, when directed opposite to the positive axis
questions.e: The sign of one-dimensional displacement indicates direction.

questions.q: Which quantity measures how fast distance is covered?
questions.e: Speed is distance traveled per unit time.

questions.q: Which quantity includes direction of motion?
Which is the SI unit of speed?
questions.e: Speed is distance divided by time.

questions.q: Which is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.e: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time.

questions.q: What is average speed?
o: Total distance divided by total elapsed time
questions.e: Average speed uses total distance, including detours.

questions.q: What is average velocity?
o: Total displacement divided by total time
questions.e: Average velocity is based on net displacement.

questions.q: What does a speedometer show approximately?
o: Average velocity for the entire trip
questions.e: A speedometer displays speed at the current instant.

questions.q: A runner completes a circular lap at constant speed. Is velocity constant?
When is velocity uniform?
questions.e: Uniform velocity requires a constant vector velocity.

questions.q: Which motion has zero acceleration?
o: Constant velocity in a straight line
Speeding up in a straight line
Moving in a circle at constant speed
questions.e: Acceleration is zero when velocity does not change.

questions.q: What is acceleration?
o: Change in velocity per unit time
questions.e: Acceleration describes the rate of velocity change.

questions.q: Can an object accelerate without changing its speed?
questions.e: Changing direction changes the velocity vector.

questions.q: A negative acceleration along the chosen positive axis means:
o: Acceleration points in the negative direction
questions.e: The sign specifies acceleration direction; slowing down depends on velocity direction.

questions.q: What is uniform acceleration?
o: Equal velocity changes in equal time intervals
questions.e: Uniform acceleration is a constant rate of velocity change.

questions.q: What is non-uniform acceleration?
questions.e: Unequal changes in velocity per equal time indicate non-uniform acceleration.

questions.q: What acceleration is used for free fall near Earth in this chapter?
questions.e: Gravitational acceleration is approximately 9.8 m/s² downward.

questions.q: At the highest point of a ball thrown vertically upward, its acceleration is:
questions.e: Gravity continues acting at the top of the trajectory.

questions.q: For a freely falling body released from rest, initial velocity is:
questions.e: Released from rest means initial speed is zero.

questions.q: Neglecting air resistance, two objects of different masses fall with:
questions.e: Near Earth both have approximately the same free-fall acceleration.

questions.q: What is plotted on the horizontal axis of a distance-time graph?
questions.e: Time is the independent horizontal variable.

questions.q: What is plotted on the vertical axis of a distance-time graph?
What does the slope of a distance-time graph represent?
questions.e: Slope equals change in distance divided by time.

questions.q: A horizontal distance-time graph represents:
questions.e: Distance remains unchanged as time passes.

questions.q: A straight rising distance-time graph represents:
questions.e: A constant slope means constant speed.

questions.q: A distance-time curve with an increasing slope indicates:
questions.e: The slope is speed, so a steeper slope means greater speed.

questions.q: A distance-time curve that becomes flatter indicates:
questions.e: A decreasing slope means speed is falling.

questions.q: Which distance-time graph shows the faster constant speed?
o: The line with smaller distance at every instant
questions.e: Greater slope corresponds to greater speed.

questions.q: What is plotted on the vertical axis of a speed-time graph?
What does the gradient of a speed-time graph give for straight-line motion with unchanged direction?
questions.e: The speed-time gradient is the rate of speed change, equal to signed acceleration for motion in a fixed positive direction.

questions.q: What does the area under a speed-time graph represent?
questions.e: Area equals speed multiplied by time, giving distance.

questions.q: A horizontal speed-time graph above zero indicates:
A speed-time graph along the time axis indicates:
questions.e: Speed is zero at every displayed time.

questions.q: A straight upward-sloping speed-time graph indicates:
questions.e: Constant positive gradient means speed increases at a constant rate.

questions.q: A straight downward-sloping speed-time graph indicates:
o: Increasing distance at an increasing rate
questions.e: A constant negative slope indicates speed falls uniformly.

questions.q: The area of a rectangle under a constant speed-time graph is:
questions.e: Rectangle area equals height times width.

questions.q: The area of a triangle under a speed-time graph is:
questions.e: The triangular area formula gives distance.

questions.q: Which quantity can never be negative?
What is the approximate universal speed limit mentioned in the chapter?
questions.e: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.q: Which phenomenon sets the universal speed limit?
questions.e: The speed of light in vacuum is the limiting speed.

questions.q: Which quantity is calculated using v = s/t?
questions.e: Speed equals distance divided by time.

questions.q: Which quantity is calculated using a = (v − u)/t?
questions.e: Acceleration equals change in velocity divided by elapsed time.

questions.q: Which equation gives final velocity for uniform acceleration?
questions.e: Rearrange a = (v − u)/t to obtain v = u + at.

questions.q: When a moving object reverses direction, which quantity definitely changes?
questions.e: Reversing direction changes the velocity vector.

questions.q: A car moves east at 12 m/s. Which statement correctly describes its velocity?
questions.e: Velocity must include speed and direction.

questions.q: Why can average speed differ from average velocity magnitude?
questions.e: Average speed uses total distance, whereas average velocity uses net displacement.

questions.q: What is the gradient of a horizontal speed-time line?
questions.e: A horizontal line has zero vertical change.

questions.q: How is speed converted from km/h to m/s?
How is speed converted from m/s to km/h?
What does a nonzero slope on a speed-time graph indicate?
questions.e: Nonzero slope means speed varies with time.

questions.q: Which pair contains only vectors?
questions.e: Both velocity and acceleration have direction.

questions.q: Which pair contains only scalars?
questions.e: Both distance and speed have magnitude only.

questions.q: A stone falls vertically from rest. How does its speed change (ignoring drag)?
o: It increases by about 9.8 m/s each second
It decreases by 9.8 m/s each second
questions.e: Free fall has approximately constant acceleration of 9.8 m/s².

questions.q: For an object thrown upward, which direction is gravitational acceleration?
questions.e: Gravity points downward during ascent, at the top, and during descent.

questions.q: What is the main difference between instantaneous and average speed?
o: Instantaneous speed is at one moment; average covers an interval
questions.e: Instantaneous speed refers to an instant; average speed to a full interval.

questions.q: What does the symbol Δ usually indicate in motion equations?
questions.e: Δ indicates final value minus initial value.

questions.q: If a car slows while traveling east, its acceleration points:
questions.e: Acceleration opposes eastward velocity during slowing.

questions.q: If a car speeds up while traveling west, its acceleration points:
questions.e: Acceleration is in the direction of increasing westward velocity.

questions.q: Which motion can have constant speed but changing velocity?
What does a steeper speed-time graph indicate in magnitude?
o: Larger rate of change of speed
questions.e: Steeper slope means a larger acceleration magnitude for straight-line motion.

questions.q: Which is needed to specify a velocity completely?
questions.e: Velocity is a vector and requires direction.

questions.q: For a complete round trip, average velocity is:
questions.e: A round trip has zero net displacement.

questions.q: In a distance-time graph, a straight line with greater gradient shows:
questions.e: Speed equals the slope of distance versus time.

questions.q: Which measurement is needed with distance to calculate average speed?
questions.e: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

questions.q: In uniform acceleration, what remains constant?
o: Change in velocity per unit time
questions.e: Constant acceleration means the rate of velocity change is constant.

questions.q: What is the speed of an object that remains at the same position?
questions.e: An object at rest covers no distance per unit time.

questions.q: Which describes the displacement of a body moving 5 m north?
A speed-time graph has zero area over an interval. What is the distance traveled?
questions.e: Area under a speed-time graph gives distance.
